tip: After sense verbs like пахнет (pakhnet = smells), Russian uses an adverb, not an adjective: пахнет замечательно (pakhnet zamechatelno = smells wonderfully).
Exclamations use какой (kakoy = what a), agreeing with the noun. Neuter здание (zdaniye = building) takes the neuter form Какое (Kakoye).
Feelings put the person in the dative: мне холодно (mne kholodno = I am cold), literally to-me cold. Also тепло (teplo = warm), грустно (grustno = sad).
With понравился (ponravilsya = appealed) the thing liked is the subject and the liker goes in the dative: Отцу понравился ресторан (Ottsu ponravilsya restoran = to father appealed the restaurant).
нужен (nuzhen = needed) agrees with the thing needed, not the person: masculine телефон (telefon = phone) gives Брату нужен телефон (Bratu nuzhen = brother needs).
много (mnogo = many) is followed by the genitive plural: много проблем (mnogo problem = many problems), not the plain plural проблемы (problemy).
Clock times use в plus the accusative number: в одиннадцать (v odinnadtsat = at eleven). No extra word for at is added beyond в.
на углу (na uglu = on the corner) is a street corner outside; в углу (v uglu) is an inside room corner. Same noun угол (ugol), different preposition.
о (o = about) becomes об before a vowel sound: об интересном фильме (ob interesnom filme = about an interesting movie).
Names use зовут (zovut = they call), a they-form with no subject: как вас зовут (kak vas zovut), literally how you they-call = what is your name.
без (bez = without) takes the genitive: без хорошего образования (bez khoroshego obrazovaniya = without a good education).
For an action still going on, Russian uses the present with уже (uzhe = already): ждём уже двадцать минут (zhdyom uzhe dvadtsat minut = have been waiting twenty minutes).
Animate masculine accusative copies the genitive form: этого человека (etogo cheloveka = this person), because a person is the object, not этот человек (etot chelovek).
назад (nazad = ago) comes after the time span, not before it: пять лет назад (pyat let nazad = five years ago).
covered with uses the instrumental with no preposition: покрыта снегом (pokryta snegom = covered with snow), no separate word for with.
Поздравляю (pozdravlyayu = congratulations) takes с plus the instrumental: с повышением (s povysheniyem = on the promotion).
Dates put day and month in the genitive: Восьмого марта (Vosmogo marta = the eighth of March), literally of-the-eighth of-March.
